'''Sana Shrine''' (佐那神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Taki, Mie|en|Taki, Mie|qid=Q1203963|lt=Taki Town}}, {{ill|Taki District, Mie|en|Taki District, Mie|qid=Q1042360|lt=Taki District}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}, Japan. The shrine has historical ties to the [[Ise Grand Shrine]] and is associated with {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|en|Ame-no-Tajikarao|qid=Q849412|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Mikoto}}, who is also enshrined as a [[secondary deity]] at the Ise Grand Shrine.

== name and Etymology ==
The name "Sana" originates from the place name "Sana-no-agata" mentioned in ancient texts like the ''[[Kojiki]]'' and ''[[Kotaijingu Gishikicho]]''.<ref name="sk1">''Shikinaisha Kenkyukai,'' 1990, p. 411.</ref> In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the shrine was popularly called "Ōmori Shrine" or "Nakamiya."<ref name="sk1"/> The name "Nakamiya" is believed to relate to its status as one of three prominent shrines in the region, alongside Sumaru-me Shrine (Ichinomiya) and {{ill|Kushida|en|Kushida |qid=Q1794549|lt=Kushida Shrine}} (Taisha).<ref name="sk1"/>

== Enshrined Deities ==
The shrine primarily enshrines the following two deities:<ref name="sk1"/>
* {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|en|Ame-no-Tajikarao|qid=Q849412|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Mikoto}}
* [[Akebono-Tatsu-O|Akebono-Tatsu-O-no-Mikoto]]

Ame-no-Tajikarao is mentioned in the ''Kojiki'' as residing in "Sana-no-agata," while Akebono-Tatsu-O is described as the ancestor of the [[Sana clan]].<ref name="sk1"/>

Additional deities from merged shrines include:<ref name="sk1"/>
* [[Ame-no-Uzume]]
* [[Kumano Gongen|Hayatama-no-Mikoto]]
* {{ill|Izanami|en|Izanami|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami}}
* [[Amaterasu]]
* [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]]
* [[Ame-no-Oshihomimi]]
* [[Ame-no-Hohi]]
* [[Amatsuhikone]]
* {{ill|Ikutsuhikone|en|Ikutsuhikone|qid=Q11147583|lt=Ikutsuhikone}}
* [[Kumanokusubi|Kumano-Kusubi]]
* [[Tagitsuhime]]
* [[Tagorihime]]
* [[Ichikishima-hime]]
* [[Kagu-tsuchi|Kagutsuchi]]
* [[Ukanomitama]]
* [[Ōyamatsumi|Ōyama-tsumi]]
* [[Konohanasakuya-hime]]
* [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|Koto-shiro-nushi]]
* [[Hachiman]]
* [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko]]
* {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|en|Sugawara no Michizane|qid=Q382005|lt=Sugawara no Michizane}}

== History ==
The exact founding date of the shrine is unknown, but it is listed in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' (927) as a minor shrine (小社).<ref name="sk2">''Shikinaisha Kenkyukai,'' 1990, p. 412.</ref> The shrine's main hall has historically been rebuilt using materials donated from the [[Ise Grand Shrine]] during its [[Jingū Shikinen Sengū|Shikinen Sengu]] reconstruction.<ref name="sk2"/>

In the Edo period, the shrine received official recognition as a ''Shikinaisha'' and was referred to as "Sana Shrine" on a stone marker erected in {{ill|1724|en|1724|qid=Q6926|lt=1724}}.<ref name="sk2"/> It was promoted to a prefectural shrine in {{ill|1943|en|1943|qid=Q18623|lt=1943}}.<ref name="sk2"/>

== Festivals ==
The shrine hosts monthly rituals on the 1st and 15th of each month, as well as annual festivals including:<ref name="sk3">''Shikinaisha Kenkyukai,'' 1990, p. 413.</ref>
* January 1: New Year's Festival
* February 8: ''Kinen'' Festival
* June 30: Summer Purification
* October 8: festival
* December 30: Year-End Purification

== Cultural Significance ==
The shrine is regarded as the guardian of the former [[Sana Village]], covering several districts in modern [[Taki Town]]. The deity Ame-no-Tajikarao is worshiped as a god of strength, attracting visitors from {{ill|Matsusaka|en|Matsusaka|qid=Q460829|lt=Matsusaka}}, {{ill|Kameyama|en|Kameyama|qid=Q448668|lt=Kameyama}}, and as far as {{ill|Nagoya|en|Nagoya|qid=Q11751|lt=Nagoya}} and {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|qid=Q35765|lt=Osaka}}.<ref name="tkp">Mie Prefectural Oka High School Newspaper Club, 2011, p. 1.</ref>

== Transportation ==
The shrine is located near [[:en:JR Central|JR]] {{ill|Kisei Main Line|en|Kisei Main Line|qid=Q582803|lt=Kisei Main Line}} {{ill|Sana Station|en|Sana Station|qid=Q265438|lt=Sana Station}}, approximately a 10-minute walk away.<ref name="mkr">Mie Tourism Association, accessed November 2, 2013.</ref> It is also accessible via {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kotsu}} bus from the "Gokeiguchi" stop.<ref name="tkp"/>
